thread:
maria: seeing huge latency + cost spikes for single large-vec requests (~1.2MB, 8192 dims). console shows per-route qps fine but per-request cost exploded. anyone seen this?

 todd: can you paste headers + dims? also route id and trace id?

 maria: route=embeds-1, trace=trace-9c3, dims=8192, content-length=1240192, sdk=python-0.4.2

 jing: hmm large single vectors will prevent batching and hold the router's inflight slot for long. current router favors coalescing small requests into batches -> big one stalls window

 sam: possible solutions: 1) fastpath direct to worker if payload_bytes > X; 2) split big single vector into smaller chunks (but that changes semantics); 3) size-aware priority queue that deprioritizes big requests

 kevin: we should avoid changing API semantics. propose size-aware routing policy config. example:

 ```yaml
 route: embeds-1
 routing:
   size_fastpath: true
   fastpath_threshold_bytes: 256000
   preserve_quota: true
   max_concurrency_fastpath: 2
 ```

 sam: preserve_quota important. if fastpath bypasses router, we still need to debit quota and enforce per-tenant concurrency

 maria: console UX: ops can't tell which requests are "fastpath" vs normal. we need a payload_size bucket chart and a tail-latency by size bucket.

 console-bot: created dashboard tile "embeds.payload_size_buckets" with count, p95_latency, and cost_per_request.

 todd: telemetry: add sample fields: size_bytes, dims, batch_wait_ms so we can correlate wait time vs size. also log route_decision=fastpath|normal

 ops-bot: note: canary config will only be enabled for dedicated clusters in next deploy. will not roll out to hosted yet.

 jing: also need SLO considerations: big single-item requests should not violate tenant fairness. maybe a soft-queue that limits concurrency rather than full bypass

 maria: agreed. let's prototype size_fastpath=opt-in + preserve_quota + telemetry flags. i'll open a PR with integration tests for quota debit and console tiles

 todd: ping @kevin for YAML schema validation and @sam for fairness test cases

 kevin: ack, will review the PR

 maria: thanks folks :thumbsup:
